name: Google Sync

releases.author: sertacyildiz
releases.description:
## Fix: Drive deletes are recoverable now

Deleting a file on Drive during sync used a permanent delete that skipped the trash — so if a sync ever removed the wrong file, it was gone for good.

- **Drive deletes now go to Drive's trash.** Anything the sync removes on Drive is recoverable from your Drive trash for ~30 days, instead of being permanently erased.
- **Local deletes were already recoverable** — they route to your OS trash (macOS/Windows), falling back to the vault's `.trash`. Unchanged.
- **GCS** deletes still depend on your bucket's Object Versioning / Soft Delete (GCS has no per-file trash). Enable one of those if you sync to GCS and want the same safety net.

This brings Drive in line with the local side's "never lose data irreversibly" guarantee.
releases.name: 0.6.2 — recoverable Drive deletes

releases.author: sertacyildiz
releases.description:
## Fix: a stuck "sync already running"

A stalled network request could hang a sync indefinitely — and the "a sync is already running" guard with it, so every later **Sync now** did nothing until you reloaded Obsidian.

- **Requests can no longer hang forever.** Each request to Google now has a 120-second ceiling. If a connection opens but never responds (dead network, captive portal, a stalled endpoint), the sync fails cleanly, the lock clears, and you can retry right away.
- **Real network problems surface instead of hiding.** A persistent stall now shows a "timed out" error rather than a silent, stuck sync.

If you ever land in the stuck state, reloading Obsidian still clears it — but it shouldn't happen anymore.
releases.name: 0.6.1 — no more stuck sync lock

releases.author: sertacyildiz
releases.description:
## Smarter conflict resolution

When the same note changed on two devices, sync now keeps the **newer** version — and never throws away the older one.

- **Newest wins, nothing lost.** If a file changed on both sides since the last sync, the more recently modified version becomes the file you see; the older version is saved beside it as a recoverable `<name>.conflict-<timestamp>` copy. Previously the local copy always won.
- **No more conflict storm on a new device.** Opening an already-populated vault on a second machine used to turn *every* matching file into a `.conflict-` duplicate. Identical files are no longer treated as conflicts — they're adopted cleanly, with no copies and no needless up/downloads.
- **Safe by default.** When the remote's modified time can't be determined, the local copy wins (as before), and the losing side is always kept as a backup — so a wrong clock can never silently lose your work.

Builds on 0.5.0's safety work (recoverable trash + mass-deletion guard).
releases.name: 0.6.0 — smarter conflict resolution

releases.author: sertacyildiz
releases.description:
## Last-synced visibility

A small, safe follow-up to 0.5.0.

- **See how fresh your sync is.** Settings now show how long ago each backend — and the vault overall — last synced ("synced 2 hours ago"). It's information only and never affects what a sync uploads, downloads, or deletes.

Builds on 0.5.0's safety work (recoverable trash + mass-deletion guard).
releases.name: 0.5.1 — last-synced visibility

releases.author: sertacyildiz
releases.description:
## Safer deletes

This release makes deletion **safe and recoverable** — the one place the plugin could previously lose data.

- **Deletions go to the trash, not gone for good.** When a sync removes a file locally it now moves it to your system trash (or the vault's local `.trash`) instead of permanently deleting it, so it can always be restored.
- **Mass-deletion guard.** If a sync would delete an unusually large number of files at once — more than `max(10, 20%)` of your synced files on either side, almost always a sign of a connection or folder problem rather than a real change — it stops and changes nothing, and tells you why.
- **"Protect local files" is now "Backup mode" (off by default).** Normal two-way sync propagates deletions across your devices as expected, with the trash + guard as the safety net. Turn on **Backup mode** only for a one-way single-device → cloud backup.

Recommended for everyone on 0.4.x.
releases.name: 0.5.0 — safe deletes

releases.author: sertacyildiz
releases.description:
**Your Drive sync now mirrors your vault's folder structure.** Files used to land flat in the sync folder; now your folders are recreated as real folders in Drive, matching your vault. (The path-length limit is gone too.) Google Cloud Storage already nested via key prefixes.

**Upgrading?** Your local files are safe — the first sync after updating uploads them into the new folder layout (it never mass-deletes). To avoid leftover copies of the old flat files, delete the old `Obsidian Sync/<vault>` contents in Drive before that first sync (or delete the `Obsidian Sync` folder and re-sync fresh).

Per-vault folders, last-synced time, Sync-now button, and one-click Connect are all included.

> Beta — use a throwaway vault and keep backups.
releases.name: Google Sync 0.4.6 (beta)

releases.author: sertacyildiz
releases.description:
- **Per-vault folders** — each vault syncs into its own subfolder (`<folder>/<vault name>`), so syncing several vaults to the same Drive/bucket never collides (the vault name is added automatically).
- **Last synced time** + a **Sync now** button in Settings.
- One-click **Connect Google Drive** — zero setup (a built-in OAuth client ships with the plugin; power users can use their own under Advanced).

> Beta — use a throwaway vault and keep backups.
releases.name: Google Sync 0.4.5 (beta)

releases.author: sertacyildiz
releases.description:
One-click **Connect Google Drive** — zero setup.

Click **Connect Google Drive** → approve in your browser → done. No client ID, no secret, nothing to paste — a built-in OAuth client ships with the plugin. Power users can still use their own OAuth client under **Advanced**.

Google Cloud Storage works the same way (OAuth or an HMAC key under its section).

> Beta — use a throwaway vault and keep backups.
releases.name: Google Sync 0.4.3 (beta)

releases.author: sertacyildiz
releases.description:
Connect Google Drive — bring your own OAuth client.

Create a free **Desktop** OAuth client in Google Cloud Console (enable the Drive API; publish the consent screen or add yourself as a test user), then enter its **Client ID + Client secret** under **Settings → Advanced**. Your credentials stay on your device — never synced, never committed to this repo (GitHub blocks bundling OAuth secrets, so each user supplies their own). Then click **Connect Google Drive** → browser consent → done.

Google Cloud Storage works the same way (OAuth or an HMAC key under its section).

> Beta — use a throwaway vault and keep backups.
releases.name: Google Sync 0.4.2 (beta)

releases.author: sertacyildiz
releases.description:
**One-click "Connect Google Drive" is now live.**

Click **Connect Google Drive** → your browser opens Google's sign-in → approve → done. No setup, no client ID to paste — a built-in OAuth client ships with the plugin (PKCE, no secret). You can still use your own OAuth client under **Advanced**.

Google Cloud Storage is unchanged — connect via OAuth or an HMAC key under its section.

> Beta — please test with a throwaway vault and keep backups.
releases.name: Google Sync 0.4.1 (beta)

releases.author: sertacyildiz
releases.description:
A simpler, more practical setup.

- **Two independent backends.** Enable Google Drive, Google Cloud Storage, or **both at once** — your vault syncs to each (with its own state).
- **One-click Connect, no passphrase to start.** Bring-your-own OAuth client, GCS HMAC keys, and end-to-end encryption now live under **Advanced**.
- **Google Drive** works with any Google account (no Google Cloud needed); folder defaults to `Obsidian Sync`. **Google Cloud Storage** syncs to your own bucket.
- Renamed to **Google Sync**.

> Beta: the built-in one-click sign-in is still being finalized — for now, connect using your own OAuth client ID under **Settings → Advanced**. Please test with a throwaway vault and keep backups.
releases.name: Google Sync 0.4.0 (beta)

releases.author: sertacyildiz
releases.description:
Google Cloud Storage now has a one-click **OAuth "Connect"** option, alongside HMAC keys.

- Reuse your own OAuth client (now shared by Drive + GCS) and connect with a browser consent — no HMAC key needed for GCS.
- **HMAC stays the recommended, least-privilege path.** A GCS OAuth token (`devstorage.read_write`) can reach every bucket your Google account can access — GCS has no per-bucket OAuth scope — so the UI says so; prefer HMAC, or a Google account/project scoped to just your bucket.
- OAuth tokens are treated like any credential: never synced, optionally passphrase-encrypted at rest.

Beta — test with a throwaway vault and keep backups. Install via BRAT: `sertacyildiz/obsidian-google-sync`.
releases.name: Google Cloud Sync 0.3.0 (beta)

releases.author: sertacyildiz
releases.description: Beta. Passphrase is now OPTIONAL (default off) — connect with no passphrase wall; set one only for E2EE or to encrypt the stored credential. GCS verified end-to-end; Drive via your own OAuth client. Install via BRAT: add 'sertacyildiz/obsidian-google-sync'. Use a throwaway vault first; keep backups.
releases.name: Google Cloud Sync 0.2.0 (beta)
